newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Troops challenge Taleban in key Afghan pass.
newsitem.headline: Troops challenge Taleban in key Afghan pass.

text.p: Government forces loyal to ousted government military head Ahmad Shah Masood took the fight to insurgent Taleban troops on Friday along a vital stretch of highway between Kabul and the Salang Pass, witnesses said.

"The highway between here and Kabul is chaotic. Taleban hold some parts and we hold other parts, especially the high ground," said Abdul Bashir Salanghi, a commander of Masood's who spoke to reporters in Olang, just south of the strategic Salang Pass.

"There is still fighting in Jabal-os-Saray and in Charikar. We hope that by tomorrow we will have both places but we can't say that we have them today. Taleban were less than 5 kms (3.1 miles) from here. You can hear the shelling," Salanghi said.

Already suffering the worst military reverses in their two- year existence, the Taleban have been hit by an alliance between Uzbek chief Abdul Rashid Dostum, Masood and Karim Khalilli of the Shia Moslem Hezb-i-Wahadat.

One of Dostum's commander was asked by reporters why Masood troops had made so much progress. "The Taleban were so cruel that ordinary people have begun to fight them. This is not just Masood's forces. It is Masood plus citizens in the Salang pass," he said.
